arguments: You are an independent source-grounded red-team reviewer. Use no tools. Output the requested JSON only.

attacks.title: asserted() treats a keyword clause as authority for the act, without binding it to the subject or target of the row
source_references: engine_source.py L120-135 asserted(): acts regex, negatives, clause split, hypothetical/quote/unfinished filters
engine_source.py L429-432 primary set; deceased/wrong_number finish before any phase gate
brief-a L35 rule 9 (the person says the customer has died)
speak extraction_schema/0 description C7-C8 (only complete positively asserted primary intents)
attacks.setup: Recipient phase, unverified. Call variables title=Mr, last_name=Reyes.
raw_turns: Agent: Hello, I am a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and this call is recorded. Am I speaking with Mr Reyes?
Caller: His mother passed away last week; he is at the funeral, call tomorrow.
attacks.producer_conformance: Grammar is valid: k and c are present, the kind is advertised and there is a single END. The row is a semantic producer violation, because the deceased person is a relative, not the customer. The engine-side defect is independent of that: asserted() only checks that some clause matches the act regex and lacks if/would/quote/negation markers. It never checks the grammatical subject, the person or the product.
attacks.failure_path: decode OK. Not verified, so no accumulate. asserted(): the clause 'his mother passed away last week' matches 'passed away', has no hypothetical, negative or unfinished marker, and returns True. primary={'deceased'}. L432 runs finish('not_reached','deceased'), then farewell, then close_call with outcome not_reached/deceased. The correct handling was third-party (callback) or clarification.
attacks.expected_observable: close_call body {customer_id, outcome:not_reached, reason:deceased} instead of the callback question.
positive_controls: 'If he died you would know' gives row deceased c=1; the clause contains if/would, so it is skipped and blocked_primary asks for clarification. The repair holds.
'He has not died, he is at work' is skipped by the negatives regex.
'He passed away.' with k=deceased|c=1 correctly closes as deceased.
attacks.witness_plan: Run the CPU harness on engine_source with vars state={}, then a user turn using the rows and raw above. Assert vars.outcome=='deceased'. Repeat with 'My wife is sick, but I can pay' and a k=hardship row: hardship regex 'sick' matches, so hardship is primary even though the subject is a third person. Treat both as conditional on producer emission.
attacks.claim_limit: Keyword authority is a source fact. Actual occurrence depends on the hosted extractor emitting the violating row, which is unobserved.

attacks.title: consent_blocked() does not normalize the typographic apostrophe, so curly-quoted contracted negations bypass the consent guard
source_references: engine_source.py L173-176 consent_blocked: no replacement of the curly apostrophe; blockers list can't/don't/won't
contrast L98 recipient_reply and L126 asserted, which both normalize the curly apostrophe
engine_source.py L509-527 consent branch to commit_next
attacks.setup: Verified. One product is agreed. phase=confirm and readback is set from advance() at L265.
raw_turns: Agent: Please confirm: personal loan, 213.00 on 2026-10-16. Do you confirm?
Caller: Yes, I won’t manage that date.
attacks.producer_conformance: Grammar is valid. Emitting a bare confirm on a qualified or negative reply is a semantic violation of the prompt ('qualified yes is a correction'). Even so, consent_blocked is the defense-in-depth gate for exactly this case.
attacks.failure_path: low='yes, i won’t manage that date.' The regex \bwon't\b needs an ASCII apostrophe and does not match. 'not', 'no', 'but' and the other blockers are absent, so consent_blocked returns False. unfinished is False. consent_terms is True (no a/d). The target set equals the agreed set, so s['consent']=readback and commit_next writes create_promise with the old terms.
attacks.expected_observable: A create_promise body for the old date after a negated reply. The ASCII spelling 'won't' instead routes to advance() and a re-readback.
positive_controls: 'Yes I don't mind go ahead' (ASCII): the idiom is stripped, nothing blocks, and consent commits. The B-next2 witness is repaired.
'I don't mind, but not the date' is blocked by but/not.
'No problem' is stripped and consent is given.
attacks.witness_plan: CPU harness at the confirm state. Feed the two raw variants (U+2019 and ASCII). Assert route=='create_promise' versus 'speak'. Also test 'I don’t mind' (curly): it is not stripped but is also not a blocker, so it passes, which is benign.
attacks.claim_limit: A static lexical gap. Whether the hosted extraction preserves curly apostrophes in raw_speech is unobserved.

attacks.title: create_promise HTTP 500, explicit ok:false and missing outcome are separated; retry uses identical terms; unknown outcome stops through safe_close
source_references: openapi 500: 'Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated.'
brief-a L91 rule 37; brief-b L19 rule 11
C67 create_promise post hook sets http_status
pre hook sets api_data '{}' and api_receipt
engine L291 write guard (consent token, writes<2)
attacks.setup: Exact consent recorded. Engine routes create_promise with writes=1 and request_id=N.
attacks.producer_conformance: Grammar is valid and semantically conforming.
attacks.failure_path: (a) HTTP 500: the post hook gives d={'http_status':'500',...} with no ok key. L358 is false, writes<2 holds, and commit_next runs again. consent is untouched, so the token is still present. The same product_id, amount and date go out with request_id N+1. A second 500 or an explicit ok:false marks service_error, then add_note service_error, then close. (b) Missing or unknown outcome (hook not run, or status other than 500 without ok): payload '{}', so consent is cleared, unknown_write_outcome is set and route is safe_exit. engine has no safe_exit equality, so it falls through to the always transition into safe_exit, then safe_close. The forced pre-hook (if True) computes promise if any product is recorded, otherwise no_promise/service_error. No blind retry and no recorded claim.
attacks.expected_observable: At most two create_promise bodies with identical terms. No 'recorded' sentence without ok:true. Exactly one close_call.
positive_controls: Stale receipt (signal mismatch) clears consent and asks again, with a limit of 2.
Engine sandbox failure goes engine_failure, then safe_close, then end, so the static failure route still ends through close.
attacks.witness_plan: Run the CPU harness on engine_source with synthetic payloads {'http_status':'500'}, {'ok':'false','http_status':'200'} and {}. Assert route and vars body. Read safe_close pre_process statically.
attacks.claim_limit: Whether the platform runs the post hook on a 500 is unobserved. The prior PUB12 ResultParseError root cause is unknown and is not attributed here. This is not a delivery claim.

architectural_proposals: Bind primary acts to a subject/target field in the row (e.g. who=customer|relative), and require that field for deceased, hardship and wrong_number. Keyword clauses should only veto, never authorize.
Normalize text once (Unicode apostrophes and quotes, NFKC) before every lexical guard, including consent_blocked, unfinished and the paid 'full' heuristics.
Have consent require a dedicated row form, for example confirm with an echoed readback serial, rather than lexical absence of negation.
Keep the explicit 500/ok:false/unknown tri-state, and assert the post-hook presence marker before trusting the 500 branch.

guard_assessments.recipient_vs_identity: Holds. A recipient-phase yes/answer/confirm needs recipient_reply(raw) to match exactly (e.g. 'Sofia Almeida'). It only sets phase=dob. verified is set only on an all_verified receipt.
guard_assessments.primary_completion: Partially holds. Clause-scoped if/would/quote/negation filtering repairs the B-next2 whole-turn block. Subject binding is missing (B11-01).
guard_assessments.finite_codec: Holds. amountval uses a digits regex and rejects non-finite values. dateval rejects fragments. Row grammar is strict and END-terminated.
guard_assessments.component_state: Holds statically. accumulate gathers facts from immutable rows, so a c0 u=date amount plus a complete d sibling merges regardless of row order. Conflicts trigger scoped clarification.
guard_assessments.qualified_consent: Mostly holds. ASCII idiom stripping works. The curly-apostrophe negation bypass is open (B11-02).
guard_assessments.receipt_binding: Holds. Each request gets a serial, the awaited operation is checked, a consumed receipt is rejected, and stale receipts clear consent.
guard_assessments.failure_final_close: Holds. safe_exit and engine_failure both route to safe_close with a state-derived outcome. Farewell routes to close_call.

limitations: Source-only review; nothing executed; hosted extractor, sandbox and ledger unobserved.
B11-01 and B11-02 require semantically nonconforming producer rows.
Prior B-next2 scores (8/9, PUB12rep1 ResultParseError) are preserved and not re-attributed.
transport_guard.py was read as provenance only.

Actual customer death closes, hypothetical/negated forced rows remain blocked. Row syntax alone is not authority for subject identity. No hosted/extractor evidence.

Illness of a relative is not independently established as a hardship violation by BriefA32; do not infer that from this death/recipient counterexample.
Suggested who field is not in advertised decoder; adding it requires paired versioned producer/consumer/schema changes.

supported_next_remedies.action: Normalize Unicode apostrophes/quotes consistently before scoped guards. Preserve actual negation, withdrawal and changed terms; affirmative idiom removal must remain clause-bound and never grant consent merely because blockers are absent.

Distinguish completed polite requests from hypothetical acts, and support semantically equivalent explicit stop requests. Keep c0/quoted/negated and recipient-vs-identity guards. Use subject/target scope tied to extracted clause; adding new coordination fields requires paired producer/consumer/schema versioning.

Keep immutable per-row fact reconciliation, both-order completion, latest amount and deferred-refusal clearing. Preserve exact readback tokens, fresh later consent, paid sibling isolation, authoritative identity, documented500 one retry, unknown-outcome stop and mandatorySMS only after ok.

Bind asynchronous receipts to immutable dispatched operation/request context rather than current ambient requestID if transport actually permits overlap. First establish callback/hook/template delivery semantics using hosted evidence owned by parent.
